references.text: In [ref:Esek 36:25-27|Ezekiel 36:25-27], God promises to cleanse His people and give them a new spirit and a new heart. This is the prophetic background for what Jesus says about the necessity of being born again—a divine renewal that Nicodemus, as Israel's teacher, should have known.

In [ref:Joh 3:3|John 3:3], Jesus states for the first time that no one can see the kingdom of God without being born again. Verse 7 repeats and emphasizes this necessity with the words "You must be born again" (δεῖ ὑμᾶς γεννηθῆναι ἄνωθεν), and asks Nicodemus not to be surprised by this.

[ref:Joh 3:5-6|John 3:5-6] explains what it means to be born again—to be born of water and the Spirit. What is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit. Verse 7 summarizes this and states that this new birth is an absolute necessity.

[ref:1 Joh 3:9|1 John 3:9] speaks of the one who is born of God and no longer lives in sin, because God's seed remains in him. This connects to the necessity of the new birth that Jesus proclaims in John 3:7.

[ref:1 Pet 1:23|1 Peter 1:23] explains that believers are reborn, not of perishable seed but of imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God. This elaborates on what it means to be "born again" (γεννηθῆναι ἄνωθεν) as Jesus says is necessary.

In [ref:Jak 1:18|James 1:18], it states that God "by His own will brought us forth by the word of truth". This confirms that the new birth is a divine act, in line with Jesus' words that man must be born from above.

[ref:Tit 3:5|Titus 3:5] speaks of how God saved us through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit. Paul here affirms the same truth that Jesus expresses in John 3:7—that rebirth is necessary and is God's work.

[ref:Joh 1:13|John 1:13] says that those who received the Word were born "not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God". This emphasizes that the new birth mentioned in John 3:7 is of divine origin, not human.

[ref:2 Kor 5:17|2 Corinthians 5:17] states that if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. This expresses the radical transformation that the new birth entails—the necessary rebirth Jesus speaks of in John 3:7.
